title: Wages, consumption and household debt
text: Over the past five years, the wage growth is about five percent, which is very weak. Meanwhile consumption has grown by about fifteen percent, which seems decent. However, housing debt has increased by about forty percent, which is unusual, but can be understandable after the wage and consumption increase. The increase in wages is far from sufficient to cover the increase in consumption. The increase in consumption is not because of the increase in income, but because people are borrowing more money to buy homes. Although people's wages increase, most of the money will go against paying household debt, because people spend a lot of money at home.
facts: The lecture compares wage growth, consumption and housing debt over five years.
Wages grew about 5%, consumption about 15%, and housing debt about 40%.
Wage growth cannot cover the increase in consumption.
Borrowing rather than income growth supports consumption, while debt repayments absorb income.
sample: The lecture compares wages, consumption and housing debt over five years. Wages rose by only about five percent, while consumption increased by fifteen percent and housing debt by forty percent. The speaker explains that income growth is insufficient to support higher consumption. Instead, people are borrowing more, especially to buy homes, and much of their additional income goes towards repaying household debt.

title: Soot and black carbon
text: Sometimes it's the little things that can make big things happen. Fleas and the plague, atoms and nuclear bombs. Diminutive leaders in world history. Soot is one of these little things. Soot, also known as black carbon, is released when you burn dung, coal, diesel fuel and wood. From Los Angeles to Mumbai, soot causes respiratory illnesses like lung cancer and asthma and contributes to one point six million premature deaths every year, mostly among the poor. And it gets worse. Atmospheric currents carry soot thousands of miles from where it is produced, to the Himalayas and the Arctic. Black carbon, being black, absorbs sunlight, so even a little soot on snow makes it melt faster. And when snow melts, global sea levels rise, threatening our freshwater, indigenous communities and polar bears who hunt on the Arctic ice. Climate change has been a big thing for a while and carbon dioxide has been its main cause. Scientists estimate that soot causes twenty-five percent of human-caused global warming. It's the second leading cause of Arctic warming after carbon dioxide. Let's not underestimate the impact of this tiny particle. But there's good news: reducing black carbon may be the fastest way to slow global warming. Buy time for the Arctic. Yes, even more so than changing a light bulb. Since black carbon only stays in the atmosphere for a couple of weeks, reducing it will produce results immediately.
facts: Black carbon or soot is released by burning dung, coal, diesel and wood.
The speaker links soot with respiratory disease and premature deaths, particularly among poorer people.
Air currents carry soot to snow-covered regions where it absorbs sunlight and accelerates melting.
The lecture describes a major contribution to warming and argues that cutting this short-lived pollutant can bring rapid benefits.
sample: The lecture explains how soot, or black carbon, has large effects despite its tiny size. Burning fuels releases soot, which contributes to respiratory illnesses and premature deaths. Atmospheric currents transport it to the Himalayas and the Arctic, where it absorbs sunlight and makes snow melt faster. The speaker also describes its contribution to global warming. Because black carbon stays in the atmosphere for only a few weeks, reducing emissions could deliver rapid benefits.

title: Civilisation as a ship
text: Our civilization, which subsumes most of its predecessors, is a great ship steaming at speed into the future. It travels faster, further and more laden than any before. We may not be able to foresee every reef and hazard, but by reading her compass bearing and headway, by understanding her design, her safety record, and the abilities of her crew, we can, I think, plot a wise course between the narrows and bergs looming ahead. And I believe we must do this without delay because there are too many shipwrecks behind us. The vessel we are now aboard is not merely the biggest of all time; it is also the only one left. The future of everything we have accomplished since our intelligence evolved will depend on the wisdom of our actions over the next few years. Like all creatures, humans have made their way in the world so far by trial and error. Unlike other creatures, we have a presence so colossal that error is a luxury we can no longer afford. The world has grown too small to forgive us any big mistakes.
facts: Civilisation is compared with a large, fast-moving ship carrying humanity into the future.
Although hazards cannot all be predicted, understanding the ship, its history and its crew can guide wise decisions.
Past failures make urgent action necessary, and this is the only vessel remaining.
Human influence is now so large that major mistakes from trial and error are no longer affordable.
sample: The speaker compares civilisation to a huge ship moving rapidly towards the future. Although not every hazard can be predicted, understanding its direction, design, history and crew can help humanity choose a wiser course. Past failures show why action is urgent. The speaker argues that the future depends on decisions made over the next few years. Human influence has become so extensive that the major mistakes once associated with trial and error can no longer be afforded.

title: Morton Prince and multiple personalities
text: Morton Prince was an American physician and psychologist; his book, Dissociation of a Personality, was the best-seller at that time. It tells the story of Miss Christine Beauchamp, who was suffering from MPD, Multiple Personality Disorder. Miss Beauchamp had several personalities, namely B1, B2 and B3. There was a hidden memory in these three personalities. Miss Beauchamp was B2. B2 knows about B1, B3 knows both B1 and B2, but B1 knows nothing about B2 or B3. The strongest personality accounts for most of the time, and it will take over the others and become the main personality at the end. This case and theory give great help to crime investigation. The Beetle, featuring menacing foreign mesmerists, hypnotising villains, somnambulistic criminals and spectacular dissociations of personality. Such figures and tropes were not merely the stuff of Gothic fiction, however; from 1875 to the close of the century, cases of dual or multiple personality were reported with increasing frequency.
facts: The lecture discusses Morton Prince, his book and the case of Christine Beauchamp.
The passage describes B1, B2 and B3 with different access to memories of the other personalities.
The speaker describes a dominant personality and a connection with crime investigation.
The passage connects dissociation with Gothic fiction such as The Beetle and increasingly frequent late-nineteenth-century reports.
sample: The lecture discusses the American physician and psychologist Morton Prince and his book about Christine Beauchamp. It describes three personalities with unequal awareness of one another: B2 knows B1, B3 knows both, and B1 is unaware of the others. The speaker also refers to a dominant personality and possible relevance to crime investigation. Finally, the passage connects these ideas with Gothic fiction and increasingly frequent reports of multiple personalities near the end of the nineteenth century.

title: Returning Tom’s book
text: You have to return a book to your friend, Tom, but when you get to school, you realize you have forgotten to bring it. Tom really needs it today. What will you say to Tom?
facts: Speak directly to Tom and explain that the book was forgotten.
Acknowledge that he needs it today and communicate a workable way to help.
sample: Hi Tom, I'm sorry, I forgot to bring your book to school, and I know you need it today. Could I go home at lunchtime and bring it back to you? If that is too late, let me know when you need it and I will try to arrange for someone to drop it off.
